deck.title: Management of Change Lifecycle Concept Cards

concepts.canonicalLabel: Change Safety and Health Impact Review

cards.backDefinition: A formal process for identifying, reviewing, approving, communicating, implementing, and documenting changes that could affect process safety. Under OSHA PSM, covered-process changes other than replacements in kind must be managed through written procedures.
cards.whyItMatters: Changes can create new hazards or invalidate existing safeguards. A controlled MOC process makes safety consequences visible before the changed process is placed in service.
cards.keyPoint: Treat change as a managed safety process, not only as an engineering or maintenance task.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(1) - Management of change
Appendix C, Section 11 - Managing Change

cards.backDefinition: Under OSHA PSM, a replacement that satisfies the existing design specification. Replacement in kind is excluded from the paragraph 1910.119(l) MOC requirement.
cards.whyItMatters: Correctly distinguishing a true like-for-like replacement from a change prevents unnecessary MOC while avoiding the dangerous practice of bypassing MOC for equipment that differs from the approved design.
cards.keyPoint: If the replacement does not satisfy the design specification, treat it as a change rather than assuming it is replacement in kind.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(b) - Replacement in kind definition
29 CFR 1910.119(l)(1) - replacements in kind exception

cards.backDefinition: The initial determination of whether a proposed modification is a change that requires the MOC process or a genuine replacement in kind that can follow normal replacement controls.
cards.whyItMatters: Early screening establishes the correct control path before work proceeds, reducing the chance that a technical, procedural, chemical, equipment, or facility change escapes formal review.
cards.keyPoint: Screen before implementation, not after the modification is already in service.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(1) - changes subject to MOC
Appendix C, Section 11 - define change before implementation

cards.backDefinition: The engineering or process rationale that explains why a proposed change is needed and the technical assumptions, design information, or operating basis supporting it.
cards.whyItMatters: A clear technical basis allows reviewers to test whether the proposed change is compatible with the process design and whether the change creates consequences that need additional controls.
cards.keyPoint: OSHA 1910.119(l)(2)(i) requires the technical basis to be addressed before the change.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(2)(i) - technical basis for proposed change
Appendix C, Section 11 - typical change form technical basis

cards.frontLabel: Change Safety and Health Impact Review
cards.backDefinition: A pre-change evaluation of how a proposed modification could affect hazards, safeguards, exposure, operating conditions, and other safety or health consequences.
cards.whyItMatters: A change that improves production or reliability can still weaken protection elsewhere. Reviewing safety and health impact before implementation helps detect those interactions while the design can still be changed.
cards.keyPoint: Assess the safety and health impact before authorizing implementation.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(2)(ii) - impact on safety and health
Appendix C, Section 11 - safety and health considerations

cards.backDefinition: The pre-change check that determines whether the proposed modification will require changes to operating procedures or practices and identifies what must be revised.
cards.whyItMatters: Equipment, process, control-system, or operating-condition changes can make existing instructions inaccurate. Identifying procedure impacts before startup prevents operators from relying on obsolete directions.
cards.keyPoint: Identify procedure changes during MOC review, then update the affected documents before they are needed.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(2)(iii) - modifications to operating procedures
Appendix C, Section 1 - operating procedure changes and MOC

cards.backDefinition: The defined approval requirement that identifies who has authority to accept a proposed change after the required MOC considerations have been addressed.
cards.whyItMatters: Formal authorization creates an accountability point between analysis and implementation, helping prevent unreviewed changes from entering the process through informal decisions.
cards.keyPoint: Approval should follow the required review, not substitute for it.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(2)(v) - authorization requirements
Appendix C, Section 11 - approvals and authorization on a typical change form

cards.backDefinition: Management of a nonpermanent change with an identified duration or time limit, monitoring, and a defined path either to restore the original condition or to process a further approved change.
cards.whyItMatters: Temporary arrangements can silently become permanent. Time limits and follow-up keep temporary conditions visible and help ensure that the process returns to its approved basis when the temporary need ends.
cards.keyPoint: Temporary changes are still changes and remain subject to MOC controls.

sourceRefs.locator: Appendix C, Section 11 - temporary changes, time limits, and return to original conditions
29 CFR 1910.119(l)(2)(iv) - necessary time period for the change

cards.backDefinition: Informing and training operating, maintenance, and contract employees whose job tasks are affected by a change before startup of the process or affected part of the process.
cards.whyItMatters: A technically sound change can still fail if people continue to work from the old configuration, limits, or procedures. Pre-startup communication and training align work practices with the approved change.
cards.keyPoint: Affected personnel must understand the change before the changed process is started.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(3) - affected employees informed and trained before startup
Appendix C, Section 1 - operating personnel oriented to procedure changes before the change

cards.backDefinition: Updating the affected process safety information when an approved change alters information that OSHA PSM requires the employer to maintain.
cards.whyItMatters: MOC is not complete if drawings, design data, chemical information, or other process safety information still describe the old configuration. Current information supports future operation, maintenance, analysis, and review.
cards.keyPoint: When the change alters required process safety information, update that information accordingly.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(4) - update affected process safety information
Appendix C, Section 11 - documentation and review of changes

cards.backDefinition: Revising affected operating procedures or practices so they accurately reflect the approved changed condition and are available for safe operation.
cards.whyItMatters: Outdated procedures can direct workers to use old steps, limits, or equipment arrangements. Updating them converts the approved change into usable operational guidance.
cards.keyPoint: OSHA PSM requires affected procedures or practices to be updated when the change alters them.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 CFR 1910.119(l)(5) - update affected operating procedures or practices
Appendix C, Section 1 - operating procedures updated before startup after process changes

cards.backDefinition: The controlled completion of an MOC after required implementation, document updates, communication or training, temporary-change disposition, and other assigned actions have been confirmed.
cards.whyItMatters: Closeout provides evidence that the approved change was carried through into the operating system rather than leaving open actions, stale documents, or temporary conditions behind.
cards.keyPoint: Close the MOC only after the required follow-through has been verified.

sourceRefs.locator: Appendix C, Section 11 - documentation, review, temporary-change restoration, and MOC follow-through
29 CFR 1910.119(l)(3)-(5) - training and information/procedure updates
